verdict.line: You win if you punish him before level 6 and close the game by the 20-minute mark; you lose if the lane drags and he free-farms into his late-game spike.

brief.thesis: Nasus' Siphoning Strike (Q) only becomes a threat if he's allowed to farm killing blows uncontested, while Darius' Hemorrhage stacks and E (Apprehend) pull punish him every time he steps forward to last-hit. The data backs this: Darius holds both lane and solo-kill advantage here, but the matchup is rated even overall because the moment Nasus stacks freely and hits his late powerspike, the fight inverts.

theirWindow.when: after level 11, if he farmed free
theirWindow.what: Once Nasus has stacked Siphoning Strike uncontested, his per-hit damage starts to eclipse yours. Don't commit to a drawn-out 1v1 on his Spirit Fire zone, and respect his R (Fury of the Sands, 120s cooldown) — it adds Health, range, and max-Health drain damage the instant it's up.

yourWindow.what: The instant he steps up to last-hit, hook him with E (Apprehend) — it passively strips Armor on your hits — then land W (Crippling Strike) to kill his retreat speed and swing Q (Decimate) twice to stack Hemorrhage to max before his Wither (15-11s cooldown) is even relevant.

start.why: Highest pick rate and win rate (51.2% over 2,840 games) — the extra early AD and sustain fund the all-in trades you need to win before he's farmed.

boots.why: Best measured win rate (53.7% over 1,297 games) — the extra Move Speed keeps you attached to him through Wither and lets you catch him before he resets to tower.

core.why: The active haste spike lets you close the gap and chain E into R before he can Wither and walk away.
Move Speed stacking closes distance in open lane and adds a burst of damage on the first hit of a trade.
Highest-winning full path (60.2% over 304 games) — the damage-over-time conversion keeps you alive through his Spirit Fire and Wither poke.

situational.when: the enemy team adds heavy magic damage alongside nasus
you need burst survivability to land your all-in safely
you need an extra gap closer to stick onto him before he disengages

runes.keystoneWhy: Ramping Adaptive Force and healing over an extended trade matches Darius' stack-then-burst pattern better than a burst keystone — you want to be winning the fight at stack five, not at stack one.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite has the highest measured win rate among run pages (52.3% over a 29.7% pick rate) — Ignite's guaranteed damage pairs with Noxian Guillotine's true-damage execute to close out early solo kills before he can trade back.

playing.title: Punish every CS attempt
playing.detail: Siphoning Strike only farms safely if he can walk up unanswered. Stand on the wave and force him to burn Wither just to last-hit.

playing.title: Hook the moment he's in range
playing.detail: E (Apprehend) passively strips Armor on your hits, so use the pull as soon as he's in the 535 range window rather than saving it — stack Hemorrhage fast while his Wither is down.

playing.title: Stack before you commit R
playing.detail: Noxian Guillotine's true damage scales per Hemorrhage stack, so land W (Crippling Strike) and at least one Q swing before you leap in.

playing.title: Don't fight on his Spirit Fire
playing.detail: His E zone strips your Armor the longer you stand in it. Finish the trade fast or pull him off the puddle first.

playing.title: Follow him to jungle camps
playing.detail: If he roams for cheap Siphoning Strike stacks, trail him and punish it — every uncontested kill compounds his late-game threat.

playing.title: Convert your lead by 20 minutes
playing.detail: Once he's past level 11 with a farmed Q, his duel power passes yours. Push the lead into objectives instead of scaling passively.

playing.title: Track his Fury of the Sands timer
playing.detail: His R (120s cooldown) adds Health, range, and max-Health drain damage. Never start a long fight inside that window unless you can burst him before the storm ramps.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and the win-rate figures above come from measured Darius vs Nasus games on the current patch (16.19.1, 2,586 games); the lane-phase and power-curve reasoning is my own read of the kit interactions.

stats.opponentTip: Do not let Nasus grow easily by constantly applying pressure in lane. Close in to fight him whenever he steps in range to kill him easily.
